meta.title: BLUE Engineering Trend Radar - Automotive (commercial vehicles)
meta.focus: Smart, sustainable and circular zero-emission commercial mobility (buses, coaches, vans, trucks)
meta.author: Sahar Rostami
meta.trl_policy: Each trend carries two maturity values. 'state_of_art.trl' is the EU TRL of the best publicly evidenced application today, justified by a demonstration or deployment. 'rd_frontier.starting_maturity' is the proposed starting maturity of the specific next step where BLUE could do R&D: a planning assumption to be validated, not a demonstrated TRL. 'evidence_status' marks whether the state-of-art TRL is 'supported' (a concrete demonstration or deployment is cited) or 'provisional' (only project plans, frameworks or partial evidence). TRL measures technical maturity only; regulatory acceptance and market adoption are recorded separately. Project goals are never treated as achieved results.

classification_policy.Core: Extends services BLUE already sells or projects it already runs.
classification_policy.Adjacent: Applies existing BLUE skills to a new application, customer or service.
classification_policy.Transformative: Could change how BLUE delivers value or earns revenue, including threats to current services.

ring_policy.Engage now: Concrete funding or customer demand within ~24 months; BLUE should act on it in the next proposal cycle.
ring_policy.Build capability: Demand expected in 2-5 years; invest in skills, tools and partnerships.
ring_policy.Monitor: Relevant but uncertain or outside BLUE's near-term role; track signals only.

trends.name: MCS-ready high-voltage powertrains for heavy-duty EVs
trends.classification_why: BLUE lists electric and high-voltage powertrain integration and thermal/multiphysics simulation as core capabilities.
trends.description: Battery-electric trucks and coaches with megawatt charging (MCS), requiring integrated design of HV architecture, battery thermal management and charging interface.

state_of_art.application: Series heavy trucks charging via MCS at up to 1 MW
state_of_art.evidence: Sept 2026: live interoperable MCS charging demo with Daimler Truck, MAN and Scania on a 1,000 kW charger; MAN states it has fitted MCS as standard for early-adopter customers since July 2026. Not yet TRL 9 at fleet scale: Milence plans 70 hubs by end-2027, with just over half MCS-capable.

rd_frontier.application: Higher-voltage, MCS-compatible modular powertrains for HDVs
rd_frontier.why: A live MCS demonstration does not establish performance and interoperability of future higher-voltage modular vehicle architectures; starting maturity is a proposal assumption, not inferred from a call existing.
rd_frontier.status: proposed starting maturity - to be validated

sources.title: Milence: Megawatt Charging impresses at IAA Transportation 2026 (14 Sep 2026)
HORIZON-CL5-2027-03-D5-05 topic (listed in call synthesis)

trends.expected_evolution_2031_2036: MCS moves from early-adopter option to the default long-haul charging interface; R&D shifts to higher-voltage, modular powertrains sized per mission.
trends.driver: HDV CO2 targets of -45% (2030) and -65% (2035) force battery-electric long-haul.
trends.barrier: Grid connection capacity and corridor charger roll-out lag vehicle availability.
trends.signpost: MCS share of public HDV chargers; award of the 2027 D5-05 projects.
trends.ring_why: A dedicated 2027 call (D5-05) and series offers from MAN create demand for HV integration and thermal engineering now.

trends.name: Battery state-of-health and remaining-life analytics
trends.classification_why: Extends BLUE's AI-based predictive maintenance and powertrain work into battery lifetime, warranty and second-life services.
trends.description: Estimating battery degradation, state of health (SOH) and remaining useful life from field data with physics-based and machine-learning models.

state_of_art.application: Commercial SOH analytics for e-bus fleets
state_of_art.evidence: Since November 2020, TWAICE battery-health analytics have been offered as an add-on to roughly 3,000 e-buses connected to the ViriCiti platform (eligible fleet; active subscriptions not disclosed). Fleet-learning SOH models validated on 25 e-buses (Fraunhofer IVI, 2023).

rd_frontier.application: Operator-independent, multi-OEM SOH/RUL with quantified uncertainty, feeding battery-passport dynamic data
rd_frontier.why: InnoBMS validated an early SOC/SOH algorithm on real cell data (<3% SOC error) with vehicle demos still in preparation; SOH FLEET (TMB Barcelona, Keolis, 2025) addressed operators' lack of transparent SOH access.
rd_frontier.status: proposed starting maturity - to be validated

trends.expected_evolution_2031_2036: SOH analytics become an expected fleet service and feed battery-passport dynamic data; value moves to OEM-independent, uncertainty-quantified remaining-life estimates for warranty and second-life.

trends.signpost: Battery-passport dynamic-data rules; InnoBMS vehicle demo results (mid-2027).

trends.name: Vehicle-specific and fleet digital twins
trends.classification_why: Digital twins and data-driven engineering are listed BLUE capabilities.
trends.description: Models that stay linked to each vehicle's hardware/software configuration and operating data, used for energy, health and lifecycle decisions. Enabling layer for T02, T04 and T06.

state_of_art.application: Subsystem digital twins of an electric minibus validated against vehicle tests
state_of_art.evidence: MINDED (Horizon IA, 2024-2027) reports a validated digital twin of the cabin, HVAC, battery and powertrain of an electric minibus, calibrated with two tests on a climate-controlled chassis dynamometer and used for predictive control (reporting period Jan 2024-Jun 2025). This supports TRL 5 (validated in a relevant environment) for single-vehicle subsystem twins. TWIN-LOOP (2025-2027) targets vehicle-specific twins for software-defined EVs but has no validated results yet. Fleet-level, cross-OEM twins remain the frontier.

rd_frontier.application: Twins for mixed commercial fleets across OEMs
rd_frontier.why: No public evidence of cross-OEM operational twins for buses/trucks.
rd_frontier.status: proposed starting maturity - to be validated

trends.expected_evolution_2031_2036: Vehicle-specific twins linked to operating data across the lifecycle become the backbone for energy, health and lifecycle services.
trends.driver: Software-defined vehicles make per-vehicle configuration and data available.
trends.barrier: No common data model across OEMs; data ownership and cost of keeping twins current.
trends.signpost: TWIN-LOOP validated use cases (end 2027); Catena-X twin standards.
trends.ring_why: Subsystem twins are validated, but fleet-level, cross-OEM twins still need data standards and partners; build the skill through T02/T06 projects rather than a stand-alone bid.

trends.name: Simulation-credible virtual validation and homologation
trends.classification_why: BLUE sells virtual validation and vehicle development up to homologation, and runs a V&V centre in Naples.
trends.description: Using credibility-assessed simulation (SIL/HIL, scenario-based testing) as accepted evidence in type approval, alongside physical tests.

state_of_art.application: Simulation toolchains with credibility assessment used as type-approval evidence for driver-assistance functions
state_of_art.evidence: UN Regulation No 171 (DCAS), in force since 22 Sep 2024 and published as EU OJ 2024/2689, allows virtual testing in system validation provided a credibility assessment per its Annex 5 is supplied to the type-approval authority. A virtual-testing amendment to UN R152 (AEBS) is reported by vendors (proposal kept a physical-test floor of at least 30%) but its adopted text was not confirmed in this review. No public type approval that relied on virtual evidence was found, so TRL 6, not 7, until such an example is cited.

rd_frontier.application: Credibility toolkits for bus/coach ADAS and automated shuttles
rd_frontier.why: Published frameworks focus on passenger-car functions; commercial-vehicle and shuttle cases are less documented.
rd_frontier.status: proposed starting maturity - to be validated

trends.name: Level-4 automated urban shuttles
trends.classification_why: B4IA targets Level 3; Level-4 defined-domain operation extends system scope and safety responsibility.
trends.description: Automated electric shuttles in defined operational domains: some controlled-site deployments run without onboard safety drivers; road pilots require case-specific conditions.

state_of_art.application: Level-4 shuttles in defined domains: driverless with remote supervision on a closed site; with onboard operator on public roads
state_of_art.evidence: Zurich Airport (9 Sep 2026): two shuttles with technology partner WeRide run fully automated on a defined route on airport premises without a safety driver onboard, monitored from a remote cockpit; employee shuttle, first weeks without passengers. On public roads, verified European pilots still keep an operator onboard: SHOW (2020-2024; 72 vehicles, 166,383 passengers, sites incl. Turin), Turin AuToMove (SAE L4 with safety driver, Oct 2025-Mar 2026), WeRide Leuven test permit (Sep 2025, safety officer onboard initially).

rd_frontier.application: Driverless, remotely supervised operation in mixed public urban traffic
rd_frontier.status: proposed starting maturity - to be validated
rd_frontier.why: Driverless operation has been shown in controlled airport conditions; scaling reliable, remote-supervised operation to complex mixed urban traffic remains an application-specific challenge.

recommended_rd.name: CircuTwin-HD
recommended_rd.problem: Whether a used traction inverter should be repaired, remanufactured, reused or recycled depends on how much life its power modules have left. Today this is judged with rule-based checks (age, mileage, fault codes). Passports carry identity data, not the thermal and electrical load history that drives power-module wear.
recommended_rd.research_question: Can a lifecycle digital twin that combines measured inverter load history, a physics-of-failure damage model with quantified uncertainty, and LCA/LCC choose better repair, remanufacture, reuse or recycling options than rule-based assessment?
recommended_rd.pilot_scope: Primary component: traction inverter of electric urban buses (power modules, DC-link capacitors). Second application: battery thermal-management system. Both are example components named in topic D5-03 Area B. The existing battery passport is referenced read-only; no new regulatory passport is built.
recommended_rd.blue_role: Work-package leader for multiphysics simulation, digital-twin architecture and engineering validation (roles BLUE lists in its Cluster 5 profile); LCA support.
methods: Define component identifiers, data model and access policy aligned with battery passport and Catena-X
Measure real-world electrical, thermal and mechanical loads on the selected components
Estimate degradation / remaining useful life with quantified uncertainty
Compare circular options on engineering feasibility, LCA and cost
Expose results through an API and demonstrate on an operating fleet
metrics: Remaining-life prediction error and calibration of its uncertainty on test modules
Share of decisions that match teardown findings, versus the rule-based baseline
Avoided material and CO2e per component under stated LCA assumptions
Data points traceable per component and cost of tracing them

primary.title: Data-driven circular economy for e-mobility ecosystem (2ZERO Partnership)
primary.fit: Area B (data-driven EV life-cycle management) is the primary fit: CircuTwin covers all four of its required activities - track and trace of representative components, real-world load measurement, API-based data management, and twin-based passports with LCA. Its remaining-life decision layer also touches Area A (component RUL and circularity strategy), but Area A additionally requires new design-for-dismantling concepts, which CircuTwin does not propose.
primary.indicative_eu_contribution: Indicative EUR 5-7M per consortium project across the topic; Area B suggests around EUR 5M. This is not BLUE-specific funding.
primary.verify: Innovation Action with lump-sum funding, EUR 24M topic budget, indicative EUR 5-7M EU contribution per consortium project (CORDIS scope: about EUR 7M for Area A, EUR 5M for Area B), planned 15 Dec 2026 opening and 14 Apr 2027 deadline, per the 2026-2027 Work Programme and consistent aggregators. Confirm final conditions on Funding & Tenders at opening.

recommended_rd.full_title: Uncertainty-aware lifecycle digital twin for circular decisions on electric-bus traction inverters

novelty.claim: A testable research gap, not a proven first. In the published descriptions of the EU projects reviewed, none states that it uses the in-service load history of EV power electronics with quantified remaining-life uncertainty to choose and audit circular decisions. This should be re-checked with project results and patents before a proposal.

related_work.name: CREDIT (Horizon Europe, 2024-2027)
related_work.what: Multi-layer digital twins, AI decision support and traceability for remanufacturing; five cases incl. automotive; targets TRL 7.
related_work.difference: Cross-industry platform; not focused on power-electronics wear physics or uncertainty in remaining life.

related_work.name: RUST2LIFE (Horizon Europe IA, 2026-2029)
related_work.what: Semantic digital twins linked to the Digital Product Passport, AI agents for triage, disassembly planning and certification, with LCA/LCC; three pilots at automotive remanufacturing sites; targets TRL 7.
related_work.difference: Closest project. Its public description covers the remanufacturing factory workflow; it does not mention remaining useful life or power electronics.

related_work.name: RESURRECTION (Horizon Europe, 2026-2030)
related_work.what: AI and robotics decision support for remanufacturing electronics; pilots incl. EV batteries; uses DPP and digital twins.
related_work.difference: Diagnosis and robotic disassembly at end of life; does not use in-service load history of traction inverters.

related_work.name: Remanufacturing-X (Horizon Europe, 2026-2029)
related_work.what: Remanufacturing DPP, data space and marketplace; pilots in textile, food, machinery, maritime, batteries.
related_work.difference: Data infrastructure and market; no EV power electronics pilot.

related_work.name: Kim, Lee, Han (PHME 2026)
related_work.what: Physics-of-failure state-of-damage metric for discrete IGBTs in EVs, validated by power cycling.
related_work.difference: Shows the damage-model building block is feasible in the lab; does not link it to circular decisions or LCA.

novelty.review_note: An earlier version of this file wrongly stated that RUST2LIFE could not be found; it was located on CORDIS (grant 101295335) and is now included.

work_plan: WP1 Data model and access: component IDs, load-history data points, access rules aligned with battery passport and Catena-X
WP2 Measurement: log electrical and thermal loads of inverters on an operating e-bus fleet
WP3 Damage and remaining life: physics-of-failure model calibrated on power-cycling tests, with uncertainty
WP4 Decision layer: compare repair / remanufacture / reuse / recycle on remaining life, LCA and cost
WP5 Demonstration: blind comparison against rule-based decisions on returned components
